speaker: Doctor
text: That is a very helpful start, but I need more details to pinpoint the cause of your ataxia. Have you noticed any changes in your vision, hearing, or coordination since the onset of these symptoms? Also, do you recall any specific head injuries or infections in your past?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for clarifying; the right-sided predominance is a crucial clue. Have you experienced any numbness, weakness, or double vision alongside your clumsiness? Additionally, have you had any recent fevers, headaches, or known infections like West Nile virus or Lyme disease?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is a vital piece of information; given your history of Crohn's disease and treatment with natalizumab, we must urgently rule out Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML). REQUEST TEST: MRI Brain with and without contrast. REQUEST IMAGES: MRI Brain axial and coronal slices. Have you noticed any new cognitive changes, such as memory loss or difficulty concentrating, in addition to your gait issues?

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: MRI Brain findings indicate lesions consistent with Progressive Multifocal Encephalopathy (PML). T1/T2 images show multifocal demyelinating lesions without gadolinium enhancement, indicative of PML.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML) secondary to natalizumab therapy. Given your Crohn's disease and recent ataxia, we must immediately discontinue natalizumab and consider switching to a different biologic agent. Do you have any active signs of infection in your gastrointestinal tract currently?
